name: data-analyst-mcp

tools.name: guide
tools.description: U.S. government statistics (Census, BLS, BEA, IRS, OPM, FRED, CDC, Treasury and more): the analyst's method for any question that needs official data. Call once at the start (the analyze prompt already holds the workflow). Topics: workflow (default), routing (which sources answer which questions), compute (compute's functions and survey standard errors), report (what a report needs, in short), style, report_patterns, report_schema (every report.json key). A long topic returns its outline: then ask for a section.

section.description: A section title (or its number) of the topic

tools.name: find_sources
tools.description: Official U.S. government data (Census ACS and PUMS, BLS, BEA, IRS SOI, OPM, FRED, CDC, Treasury, USDA and 60 more agencies): use it for any question that needs official statistics or an estimate built on them. With a question: the source packs ranked for it (a hint: split the question into measures and give each its source). Without one: every source with its agency, key need and example questions.

tools.name: source_brief
tools.description: One source's playbook (coverage, units, traps, citation), its questions_to_ask (the critical choices: ask the user those the request leaves open, then record_decisions), its key status, rules and request index. Required before fetch. The playbook's Access section (keyless and manual routes) comes on request: sections: ["Access"]. With doc: one of its reference docs (listed in docs) instead.

sections.description: Only these playbook sections, by title, e.g. ["Access"]

tools.name: request_schema
tools.description: Full parameters of named requests (from source_brief's requests), and the spec format; or search the source's catalog of datasets and series. fetch requires the schema of every request it uses.

detail.description: Long column lists and catalogs in full (default: shortened)

tools.name: record_decisions
tools.description: Record the method record in decisions.json (merged with what is there): how each critical question was settled (the user's answer, a Don't know with the resolution you chose, a skip, or why it was not asked; fetch checks the source's questions), and, in method, what the audits read. Lists replace the earlier list of the same name.

id.description: The question id from source_brief (e.g. "cdc:1"), or your own id for a general question

covers.description: Other question ids this one settles

blocking.description: What the user means (program, place, population): no default exists

request.description: settled_by_request: the user's own words that settle it

resolution.description: What you chose, for a Don't know, a skip or no_user

disclosures.description: One line per question decided without the user (or 'literature'), which the answer carries word for word

method.description: For the audits, any of: literature_search [{query, date, tool, found: [ref ids], note}] or [{unavailable: true, reason_code: "no_search_tool" | "network_blocked", reason}]; references [{id, citation, url, accessed, opened: true (after cite), used_for, quote}]; assumptions [{parameter, value, basis: empirical|literature|precedent|user|judgment, evidence, why_not_empirical, sensitivity (its exhibits/sensitivity.csv parameter, when different)}]; data_needs [{id, data, improves, effect, how_to_get, from_user}] or data_needs_note (why no data would help); audit_allow [{value, reason}] (numbers in the answer that are not statistics); dollar_basis_ok {reason}; rounding_ties_ok [{fact, reason}]

tools.name: check_key
tools.description: Whether a source's API key is set up (never shows the key) and, if not, what the user does. When a key is set up and the source has a live check, it is tested with one small call to the agency's own site: key.live.outcome is accepted, rejected (code key_rejected, with the fix), unreachable (the host did not answer; the key was not tested) or unclear. Sources without a live check say tested: false. live: false skips the call.

live.description: false: only say whether a key is set up (no call)

tools.name: fetch
tools.description: Download data from the agency into this session's workspace (CSV per request, data dictionary, README with the citation and terms, request.json with every URL made). Returns a summary (rows, columns, a few rows), the files, the citation and notes; status partial when a row cap was hit. Refuses (gate_blocked) until source_brief, request_schema and record_decisions are done for this source.

spec.description: Most sources: {"description": "...", "requests": [{"name", "endpoint", "params", "max_rows"}]}. Deep sources (bea, bls, fred, ipums, opm, treasury) have their own format: see source_brief and request_schema.

force.description: Fetch again even if the workspace has this exact request

tools.name: manual_bundle
tools.description: When this server cannot get the data (no key stored here, a host that refuses scripts, a network block): write one bundle for one or more sources with download scripts (.sh and .ps1, every request built in, any key asked with hidden input on the user's own computer) and INSTRUCTIONS.md. Then ingest the files the user downloads.

spec.description: Most sources: {"description": "...", "requests": [{"name", "endpoint", "params", "max_rows"}]}. Deep sources (bea, bls, fred, ipums, opm, treasury) have their own format: see source_brief and request_schema.

reason.description: Why the user downloads by hand (shown in INSTRUCTIONS.md)

tools.name: ingest
tools.description: Package files the user downloaded (from manual_bundle, a keyless_file, or the agency's site) like a fetch: CSVs, data dictionary, README and provenance. The same gate as fetch applies.

spec.description: Most sources: {"description": "...", "requests": [{"name", "endpoint", "params", "max_rows"}]}. Deep sources (bea, bls, fred, ipums, opm, treasury) have their own format: see source_brief and request_schema.

files.description: Paths of the downloaded files or their folder

tools.name: read_file
tools.description: A text file from this session's workspace (a fetched CSV, README, request.json): the first 20 KB, or max_bytes up to 100 KB. With match (a regular expression, case-insensitive), only the header line and the lines that match, numbered: look up variables in a codebook or data dictionary this way.

path.description: Relative to the workspace, or a path a fetch result listed

tools.name: compute
tools.description:
Run declarative steps over full workspace tables (data/<id>/<table>.csv or .parquet, earlier exhibits, published/*.csv) and save exhibits/<name>.csv with its lineage, so the rerun gate can replay it. Call it for every table the answer or report draws numbers from; never compute cited numbers by hand.
Steps, one verb each: filter, derive, select, rename, groupby with rollup (or with derive/filter for per-group windows and shares), join, pivot_wider, pivot_longer, orderby, slice, dedupe, concat, as, from; helpers fiscal_year, to_fiscal, state_codes, deflate, align_check (before joining two sources); replicate_se (survey standard errors and MOEs from replicate weights, e.g. ACS PUMS PWGTP1:PWGTP80 with sdr). Example: [{"filter": "AGEP >= 16"}, {"derive": {"fed": "COW == 5 ? 1 : 0"}}, {"groupby": ["fed"], "rollup": {"n": "sum(PWGTP)"}}].
Expressions: column names (col("a b") for odd ones), numbers, "text", + - * / % **, comparisons, && || !, c ? a : b, and the listed functions, aggregates and windows. guide("compute") has every verb's arguments, the function list and the replicate_se methods. For a big file, name the columns: {alias: {path, columns}}. Returns the columns, row count, a short preview and the file.

steps.description: The steps, in order (see the description)

from.description: The input alias the steps start from (default: the first)

packs.description: Source packs of the result (default: inferred from the inputs)

tools.name: facts
tools.description: Register every number the answer or report cites in facts.json. A table fact (add) is one cell of a saved CSV: table (exhibits/<x>.csv, data/<id>/<t>.csv or published/<x>.csv), where (the row's key values, matched to the CSV's own text) and column; its value is read from the cell. A derived fact (derived) has a derivation: written as an expression over fact names ("deaths_2024 / deaths_2020 - 1") it is computed here, so leave value out; a prose derivation needs value. Refuses empty cells and NaN, an ambiguous pack, unknown formats and units slips (a share given to pct100, millions given to usd_b ...); nothing is saved when any fact is refused. Returns each fact with its text (the value as the answer prints it: quote it exactly) and notes (rounding ties). fmt codes: raw, num:0, pct:1 (share 0-1), pct100:1 (already percent), pp:1, pp100:1, bp:0, dollars:0, thousands:-3, millions:1, billions:1, usd_b:1 (value in dollars), usd_b_scaled:1 (already billions), ratio:2, index:1, year; prefixes signed:, abs:, from_millions: ...; suffix :abs. pack is inferred from data/<id>/ or the exhibit's lineage.

headline.description: A number the answer leads with (needs a benchmark.csv row)

preliminary.description: An early estimate the agency will revise

vintage.description: The vintage, when not the latest

derived.description: Derived facts (after the table facts of this call)

headline.description: A number the answer leads with (needs a benchmark.csv row)

preliminary.description: An early estimate the agency will revise

vintage.description: The vintage, when not the latest

pack.description: Default source pack(s) for this call's facts

tools.name: rerun
tools.description: Replay every exhibit's recorded compute steps from its inputs and recompute every fact, without writing anything. Returns, per exhibit, whether the replay gives the same CSV, and per fact the stored and rerun values; reproduced is true only when everything matches. The audits run the same check with rerun: true.

tools.name: cite
tools.description: Save a page a method record cites into references/<id>.* and record it in references/opened.json, so "opened": true on that reference is backed by a snapshot the audit checks (and the quote is looked up in it). Pass text: the text your own fetch tool returned for the page; without text the server downloads it. Returns the record and the decisions.json reference entry to write.

url.description: The page's http(s) URL (the url in references)

id.description: The reference id ([@id]): letters, digits, _ and -

text.description: The page text your fetch tool returned

tools.name: handoff
tools.description: What each source delivered, read back from the workspace's provenance files: per source the route and retrieval date, the files with row counts, every caveat note and problem, and a short preview of each table (none for microdata), plus figures read from agency pages (published/). Returns text (ready-to-send Markdown: the per-source part of a data hand-off) and the same as structured data.

tools.name: write_table
tools.description: Write one of the tables the audits require that are not computed from fetched data: exhibits/benchmark.csv (measure, period, computed, published, source, url, accessed, match, note: each headline against the agency's published figure; "not checked" when none exists), exhibits/sensitivity.csv (parameter, base, alternative, headline_base, headline_alt, conclusion_changes: yes/no; the headlines are registered facts), or published/<name>.csv (a figure only an agency page publishes, as the page shows it, with source_url and accessed YYYY-MM-DD on every row). Data exhibits come from compute instead.

tools.name: audit_answer
tools.description: The release gate for a quick answer: call it with the reply exactly as you will send it, after the facts, decisions, references (cite) and exhibits/benchmark.csv are in the workspace. It saves the reply as answer.md and checks that every number in it is a registered fact as its format prints it (or a credited published figure, or in decisions.json audit_allow), that directions, years, rows and names match those facts, that dollar comparisons across years state nominal or real, the method record (questions, literature, disclosures, references opened, assumptions, sensitivity, data needs, benchmark), provenance, links (online: true requests them) and secrets; rerun: true replays every exhibit recipe and fact. Returns one line per check, the failures with their messages (verbose: every check), and "AUDIT PASSED" only when nothing fails. Send the answer only after it passes.

answer.description: The reply as it will be sent (Markdown)

rerun.description: Replay every exhibit recipe and recompute every fact

verbose.description: List every check, not only the failures

tools.name: build_report
tools.description: Build a self-contained HTML report or paper (report.html) and replication_package.zip from a report.json object (mode report: an exhibit chartbook; mode paper: prose-led). Facts are cited as {{name}} or {{name|fmt}}, references as [@id], footnotes as [^n]; exhibits name a CSV in exhibits/ and a chart {type, x, y, series, ...}. Each source's notices, Data Vintage block and redistribution rules are applied (microdata and withheld rows never enter the ZIP). Every report.json key (chart types and options, cover, notes_page, footnote scoping, clearance, replication) is listed in guide("report_schema"); guide("report") is the short form. Send the report once: later fixes are a patch (no report: the workspace's report.json is rebuilt). Returns the paths and the style score with the sentences to fix; call audit_report next.

report.description: The report.json object (title, mode, sources, at_a_glance, sections, exhibits, methods, ...). Default: the workspace's report.json

patch.description: Changes by dotted path, e.g. {"sections.0.body": "...", "exhibits.1.title": "..."}; null removes a key

tools.name: audit_report
tools.description: The release gate for a report built with build_report: facts, hand-typed numbers, exhibits, links (online: true requests them), the page (up to date, disclaimer, nothing external, no raw markup), vintage, each source's notices and audit hooks, clearances, secrets, style, chartbook structure, the method record, benchmarks and the replication package; rerun: true replays every exhibit recipe and fact. Returns one line per check, the failures with their messages (verbose: every check), and "AUDIT PASSED" only when nothing fails.

rerun.description: Replay every exhibit recipe and recompute every fact

verbose.description: List every check, not only the failures

tools.name: style_check
tools.description: Lint the prose of report.json (or the report object given) against the house style guide: percent in words, no first person, small numbers spelled out, plain words, sentence length. Returns the score (percent of sentences with no issue; target 90) and every sentence with its issues. Nothing is written into the report. build_report already returns the score and the first issues.

report.description: A report.json object; default: the workspace's report.json

tools.name: scan_secrets
tools.description: Check every workspace file (and every member of a ZIP) for an API key or credential: the value of any key this server can find, key-shaped assignments and URL parameters, and for sources that echo keys any 32-hex token. Lists file names and line numbers only, never values. Both audits run it too.

sources.description: Source ids used (default: the data/<id>/ folders)

tools.name: open_workspace
tools.description: Continue in an earlier workspace after the server restarted (a restart starts a new, empty workspace; the earlier files stay on disk). Without path: the recent workspaces with their titles and files. With path: later tools work in that workspace. Use it when a tool says report.json, facts.json or data files are missing although an earlier call made them. Local server only.

path.description: A workspace path or name from the list; omit to list them

instructions:
Live U.S. government data, fetched from the agency at call time; every result is cited.
Never answer a U.S. government data question from memory, and never estimate, simulate or "illustrate" a number:
if no source can answer, say so.

Workflow: find_sources(question) -> source_brief(id) -> ask the user -> record_decisions -> request_schema(id,
names) -> fetch(id, spec) -> compute -> facts -> audit_answer (send only after AUDIT PASSED). guide() has the
full method (framing, literature, accuracy checklist, combining sources, the answer, reports). When a question
spans agencies, source_brief's paired_with names the usual cross-checks: fetch both and compare.

Ask before you fetch. source_brief returns questions_to_ask: the choices that change a headline number. Ask
the ones the request leaves open in ONE round (at most 4 questions, each with exactly one "Don't know — decide
for me" option, your recommended option first), with your question tool when you have one. A blocking question
(what the user means: which program, place, population) that is skipped is asked once more. Record every
question with record_decisions; fetch refuses until they are settled (gate_blocked says what is missing).

Errors carry a code and a fix: follow the fix, never repeat a call unchanged, never present a failure as data.
in_progress is the exception: a long rerun continues in the background, and the same call made again waits on it.
If files an earlier call made are missing (the server restarted in a new workspace), open_workspace lists the
earlier workspaces and reopens one.
Keys are never asked for in chat: key_missing gives the user a command or page to store a key themselves.

Citations: cite page_url and the citation text with its retrieval date; copy every notice word for word.
Read the playbook's traps before interpreting a number; surface revisions, preliminary values, sampling error
and definition changes unprompted.
